newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Five foreign firms seek power deal in Bangladesh.
newsitem.headline: Five foreign firms seek power deal in Bangladesh.

text.p: Five foreign companies are expected to vie for a 300-megawatt power plant deal in Bangladesh, energy ministry officials said on Wednesday.

Officials from the firms -- AES Transpower Private Ltd and Occidental Energy Ventures Corp of the United States, Bangladesh-U.S. venture Banamco Ltd, Midlands Power International of Britain and Vander Horst Pte Ltd of Singapore -- attended a pre-bid meeting on Wednesday with Energy Minister Noor Uddin Khan and senior energy officials.
The companies were earlier shortlisted from among the 12 intending firms for the proposed gas-fired power plant near the eastern Haripur gas field.
The offers came from the foreign companies after Bangladesh opened the power sector up for private investment, both local and foreign, last year.
The officials said one of the five would be awarded the power plant contract through a tender on June 28.
The power plant is projected to be commissioned by the year 2000 and cost around $300 million, they said.
The energy minister told the meeting that the government was opening up avenues for private participation in the country's power sector.
Khan said another 100-megawatt power plant would be set up soon at northern Baghabari with private capital, and more in northern Sirajganj and southern Khulna district.
He assured the foreign firms that the government would charge reasonable prices for gas.
Power-hungry Bangladesh is now producing about 1,700 megawatts of electricity against demand of 2,100 megawatts, according to official figures.
